clue.text: Band to undress, ultimate in disgrace

parts.note: to strip is to take one's clothes off

indicators.note: the ultimate is the last, so this takes the final letter of the word disgrace

explanation.surface: A dancer's act of undressing ends in public shame.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a narrow coloured strip, a synonym of band as in a band of colour.

clue.text: Mediterranean vessel traversing small lake is poetic

indicators.note: traversing means lying across, so the vessel stretches round the lake

parts.note: a saic is a ketch of the eastern Mediterranean
a pond is a small lake

explanation.surface: A boat crossing a pond is a poetic sight.
explanation.walkthrough: SAIC is a crossword favourite for a Levantine sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Spondaic describes verse metre built from spondees, two stressed syllables, so it is a term of poetry.

clue.text: Where transport cafe is, notices one that's journeyed around

indicators.note: around means the travel word surrounds the others

parts.note: rode means travelled
ads are notices, advertisements
one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Posters advertise a roadhouse to a traveller passing by.
explanation.walkthrough: A transport cafe is a cheap British café for lorry drivers, found beside main roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Such cafés stand at the edge of a highway, so this describes their location.

clue.text: Philosopher with old books having mountain to climb

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the old books of the Bible
an alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: A thinker with ancient texts has a peak to scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the Athenian philosopher, pupil of Socrates.

clue.text: Big story about the same big health problem

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the big story goes round the Latin word

parts.note: an epic is a long, grand tale
idem is Latin for the same, used in references

explanation.surface: A major news story covers a large public health issue.
explanation.walkthrough: IDEM is the Latin for 'the same', familiar from footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a widespread outbreak of disease, a large-scale health crisis.

clue.text: Quiet merriment is organised around 1 May?

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round one
organised means put in order, so the letters of merriment is are rearranged

parts.note: the figure one as the letter I

explanation.surface: Quiet celebrations are arranged around the first of May.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of 'merriment is' wrap around I for 1. Theresa May headed the UK government, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa May is an example of a head of the British government, so the question mark signals definition by example.

clue.text: Ailing, I'd start to take new drug

indicators.note: new means freshly made, so the letters are put in a different order
the start of take is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sick patient begins on a new medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalin is a heart drug extracted from foxglove leaves.

clue.text: Indigenous people rebel endlessly under Communist dictator

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the rebel piece below the dictator

parts.note: Mao Zedong, China's Communist leader

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter

parts.note: to rise is to rebel

explanation.surface: Native people rise up endlessly under a Communist tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the Polynesian first people of New Zealand.

clue.text: Sharp Conservative has something to gain advantage

parts.note: a lever is a tool that gives mechanical advantage, or a means of influence

explanation.surface: A shrewd Tory has an angle to exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp in the sense of quick-witted and intelligent is a synonym of clever.

clue.text: A king brought by seaman to a port

indicators.note: brought by says the seaman's letters come first, leading the rest along

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch is ferried by a sailor to a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major Japanese seaport city on Osaka Bay.

clue.text: Bishop needing to phone wife maybe to prove a point

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to call one's spouse is to ring home, a wife being one person you might call there

explanation.surface: A cleric must call his wife to win an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something home is to make it clearly understood, to drive a point in.

clue.text: Bird from cage, loose, struggling under farm building

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the jumbled letters below the farm building

parts.note: a barn is a farm building

indicators.note: struggling means thrashing about, so the letters of cage loose are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bird escapes from a cage and flaps beneath a barn.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is written BARN first because 'under' places the jumbled letters below it.
explanation.definitionFit: The barnacle goose is a black-and-white Arctic goose that winters in Britain.

clue.text: Conversation sure to be rambling after party

indicators.note: after places the rearranged word behind the party

parts.note: a disco is a dancing party

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the letters of sure are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to chatter aimlessly once the party is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is formal talk or exchange of views, a synonym of conversation.

clue.text: Material provided by poet rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the poet's name is read backwards

parts.note: T. S. Eliot, the poet

explanation.surface: A poet turns down the cloth someone supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: Toile is a linen or cotton fabric, often printed, so a kind of material.

clue.text: Fie, ban diesel! Unlikely not to be done away with

definitions.text: not to be done away with

indicators.note: an unlikely arrangement is an improbable one, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A protester demands a diesel ban, and is told it will never be scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Indefeasible means incapable of being annulled or forfeited, as a right that cannot be taken away.

clue.text: Hot glow of anger in experience with BA?

indicators.note: in puts the anger inside the flight

parts.note: a flight is what one experiences with BA, British Airways
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A passenger fumes about a British Airways trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Firelight is the warm light given off by a fire in a hearth.

clue.text: One's featuring in play with no hint of eloquence being required?

definitions.text: One's featuring in play with no hint of eloquence being required?

parts.words: One's featuring in play with no hint of eloquence being required?
parts.note: describes a stage performer who appears but never has to speak a line

explanation.surface: An actor appears in a play without a single eloquent word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No hint of eloquence' reads like a critic's sneer, but it means no lines to say at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurant is a non-speaking extra on stage, or a ballet dancer in the corps.

clue.text: See this place with car

parts.note: here means this place
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: An instruction to view a spot where the car is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereford is a cathedral city and seat of a bishop, so a see.

clue.text: One worker in East going after fish oil

indicators.note: going after says these pieces follow the fish

parts.note: brill is a flatfish
one as the Roman numeral I
the ant is the crossword's stock worker
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A labourer out east follows fish oil, a picture of an oily trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliantine is a perfumed hair oil, used to make hair glossy.

clue.text: Show deference? Gosh, what a childish creature!

parts.note: to bow is to show respect
wow and gosh are both exclamations of amazement

explanation.surface: Someone bows, astonished at an infant's behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bow-wow is a child's word for a dog, so a creature in nursery talk.

clue.text: A Barchester clergyman not on the level

parts.note: Obadiah Slope is the scheming chaplain in Trollope's novel Barchester Towers

explanation.surface: A cathedral cleric is dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on the level' suggests dishonesty but is literal: tilted.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslope means at a slant, inclined, so not horizontal.

clue.text: Bird left on far side of river

indicators.note: the left letter sits beyond the river, after it

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A bird is left across the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is a blackbird or thrush, as in ring ouzel.

clue.text: Huge seat falling apart outside old lodge

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the abbreviation for old
falling apart means breaking up, so the letters of huge seat are scrambled

explanation.surface: An enormous chair collapses outside an ancient lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatehouse is the small building at an estate's entrance, which is what a lodge is.

clue.text: Expression of surprise from place lacking redemption and love

parts.note: hell is the place of the damned, beyond redemption
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A shocked exclamation in a loveless, damned place.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello can be an exclamation of surprise, as in hello, what's this?

clue.text: Possible clue to 'erod being a sinner

parts.note: 'erod is the word doer written wrongly, scrambled

explanation.surface: A cryptic setter shows a possible clue to a strange word, which reads as a sinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Work backwards: 'erod is an anagram of DOER, so the wordplay that would produce it is 'wrong DOER'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer is someone who breaks the law or moral rules, a synonym of sinner.

clue.text: What's worn by everyone going round is plain

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so on and all are read backwards together

parts.note: clothes being worn are on
everyone is all

explanation.surface: Something everyone wears is plain and simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a grassy, treeless plain of South America.

clue.text: Struggled, being weak at first, then was first after break

indicators.note: after places the leading piece behind the break
at first takes only the opening letter of weak

parts.note: a break is a rest
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: A racer was feeble early, then took the lead after a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: To have wrestled is to have fought hand to hand, grappled, struggled.

clue.text: Given map instructions, drove off

definitions.meaning: having been sent along a set course, directed
beat back and put to flight, defeated

explanation.surface: A driver given directions leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is directed along a path; the other, crushingly defeated, from rout.
